question: Do the applicable sources distinguish a send attempt, transport acceptance, endpoint delivery and human acknowledgment for a walk-in critical result?
jurisdictions_compared: AE-DU vs AE-AZ vs US/international comparators
source_evidence: S1-11.1.1 (p40); S1-11.1.3 (p40); S1-9.1.5.e (p29); AD1-PP.11.2.d (p13); G2-2.1 (p6); G3-task-status; G4-xdw-workflow-document
what_existing_sources_establish: The Dubai instrument requires clear reporting to the patient and a record of the communication. It does not define delivery, receipt or acknowledgment as distinct states.
what_remains_unclear: The instrument does not say what evidence proves the communication occurred, nor whether a transport receipt is sufficient for the §11.1.3 record.
technical_consequence: A naive implementation records 'sent' as success and closes the case; the §11.1.3 record then documents an event that may never have reached the patient.
proposed_product_control: Separate ATTEMPTED / TRANSPORT_ACCEPTED / DELIVERY_CONFIRMED / CLINICAL_ACKNOWLEDGMENT_CONFIRMED / COMMUNICATION_DOCUMENTED states with forbidden conflation combinations (INV-1, INV-2).
global_comparator: G2 Worksheet 2.1 explicitly separates 'reported' from 'acknowledged' in order tracking; G3 models a task, not a delivery.
review_needed: no - both instruments verified, but a Dubai-scoped evidentiary standard was not located

question: Does the Dubai instrument require re-communication to the patient when a walk-in result is corrected?
what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §9.1.5(g) requires a corrected result to be identified as revised, with the date and time of correction, and both versions retained. §11.1.1-11.1.3 keep applying to walk-in patients.
what_remains_unclear: No retrieved Dubai clause states explicitly that the corrected value must be re-communicated to the patient, although the Abu Dhabi comparator (AD1 PP.11.3(b)) and the US comparator (G2 2.3) both require a distinct notification for amendments. Absence in the retrieved set is not proof of absence in the instrument.
technical_consequence: An implementation may suppress re-communication because a prior acknowledgment exists.
proposed_product_control: Corrections always open a new communication workflow requiring named human approval (requires_approval) and a fresh acknowledgment bound to the new revision (INV-8).
global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.3(b) 'the laboratory communicates directly with the ordering clinician'; G2 2.3 requires notification of changed results and a visible amended flag.
review_needed: yes - manual review of DHA circulars and the laboratory's own SOP required

question: Is there a fixed acknowledgment or escalation clock for critical walk-in results?
what_existing_sources_establish: Both instruments delegate timing to the organisation: DHA requires a critical-results policy and an internally defined turnaround time; the Joint Commission requires written procedures stating 'the acceptable length of time between the availability and reporting'.
what_remains_unclear: No numeric clock is fixed by either instrument. The retrieved set does not establish what a 'timely' communication means for a walk-in result.
technical_consequence: A system that hardcodes a deadline would be inventing a requirement.
proposed_product_control: The clock and escalation window live in an explicit institutional profile, labelled PRODUCT_DESIGN_CONTROL, and are shown as such in the UI and the audit record.
global_comparator: G1 EP1 requires the organisation to define the acceptable length of time rather than setting a universal limit.
review_needed: no - but the facility must still adopt and document its own clock

question: What authorises an alternative channel or alternative recipient when the primary channel fails?
what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §9.3.4 requires electronic laboratory reports to be secured; §9.3.3 addresses electronic signature and telephone provision of critical information to a physician. The Abu Dhabi comparator delegates the means of notification to the facility.
what_remains_unclear: No retrieved Dubai clause states which alternative channel may be used for a walk-in patient, who may authorise it, or what must be recorded. The documented search did not locate such a clause; this is not evidence that none exists.
technical_consequence: An implementation may silently switch to an unverified phone number or portal, creating a confidentiality and identity risk.
proposed_product_control: INV-9: alternative channels are blocked unless verified evidence or an explicitly approved institutional procedure authorises them; the authorising reference is recorded.
global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.2(c) defines the means of notification in facility policy, showing the comparator also delegates rather than mandates.
review_needed: yes - this is the strongest candidate gap for a facility-level review

question: Which results may be communicated directly to a walk-in patient?
what_existing_sources_establish: §13.4 states genetic results shall not be communicated to patients directly and shall be directed to the referring/treating physician; Appendix 3 lists genetics as requiring a prescription, which excludes it from the walk-in category in §11.1.
what_remains_unclear: The two provisions appear to conflict only when §11.1 is read without its scope. The conflict resolves on reading: genetic testing is outside the walk-in category.
technical_consequence: A system that matches on keyword relevance alone will retrieve §11.1 for a genetic result and communicate directly to the patient.
proposed_product_control: Scope gate: the policy agent returns scope_permitted=false with a §13.4 citation; the deterministic gate blocks any transmission for that scope and escalates.
global_comparator: n/a - the conflict is internal to the Dubai instrument
review_needed: no - resolved by scope; retained as a documented apparent conflict

question: Is there a UAE-wide instrument that harmonises critical-result communication across emirates?
what_existing_sources_establish: Dubai and Abu Dhabi each publish their own laboratory standards with different recipient models (walk-in patient vs responsible clinician) and different read-back provisions.
what_remains_unclear: No national harmonising instrument was located in this search. The DHA circular index could not be enumerated programmatically; this is an unverified search, not a finding of absence.
technical_consequence: A multi-emirate deployment cannot reuse one rule set; jurisdiction must be a first-class input.
proposed_product_control: Jurisdiction is stored on every case and every source; the retriever filters by jurisdiction and the audit agent flags any binding citation from outside the case jurisdiction.
global_comparator: None located - no comparator establishes cross-jurisdiction equivalence.
review_needed: yes - requires manual search of DHA and DoH publications and federal health legislation

question: Does an acknowledgment of an earlier revision satisfy the requirement for a corrected revision?
what_existing_sources_establish: The instrument requires a record of the communication and identification of the corrected report as revised. Nothing retrieved addresses whether an earlier acknowledgment transfers.
what_remains_unclear: Whether a corrected value that contradicts what the patient already acted on requires a fresh acknowledgment is not settled by the retrieved text.
technical_consequence: An implementation may treat the case as closed because 'the patient already acknowledged'.
proposed_product_control: No transfer: the acknowledgment must be bound to the current revision (INV-8); the configuration is explicit and testable in S2 and S5.
global_comparator: G2 2.3 requires notification of amended results with a visible amended flag, consistent with a fresh notification event.

question: Does an acknowledgment establish that the patient understood the advice to seek medical care?
what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §11.1.2 (guidance) directs the laboratory to advise the patient to seek further medical advice. The Abu Dhabi comparator requires read-back for verbal and telephone results.
what_remains_unclear: No retrieved source defines what evidence would demonstrate comprehension for a written channel such as SMS or a portal message.
technical_consequence: A system may present 'acknowledged' as if it meant 'understood and acted on'.
proposed_product_control: The UI states explicitly that acknowledgment means the message was opened and confirmed by a named human, not that it was understood; the case cannot record clinical resolution.
global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.4(b) read-back requirement exists for verbal/telephone only.
review_needed: no - a product-boundary statement, not a policy gap

question: What must a laboratory do to verify that a contact number belongs to the patient before sending a critical result?
what_existing_sources_establish: S1 requires secure electronic reports and a record of the communication.
what_remains_unclear: No retrieved clause specifies identity binding for a mobile number, or what to do when the number is shared or stale. The search did not locate such a requirement.
technical_consequence: A message may reach the wrong person, and the record will still look complete.
proposed_product_control: Contact reference is stored separately from the patient reference; an unverified-recipient state can be raised; the gate refuses sends whose recipient is not verified in the profile.
global_comparator: AD1 PP.11.2(d) requires identification of the individual notified, which presupposes identity verification.

question: Do existing interoperability standards model a patient acknowledgment of a critical walk-in result as a first-class event?
what_existing_sources_establish: FHIR Task provides a work-item status vocabulary; IHE XDW provides a workflow document that maintains a historical record of tasks and expects actors to handle race conditions.
what_remains_unclear: Neither retrieved profile defines an event type meaning 'the patient confirmed receipt of this specific result revision'. Task 'completed' refers to the task, not to a human understanding a result.
technical_consequence: Integrations may map a 'completed' task onto a clinical acknowledgment, which the standards do not warrant.
proposed_product_control: ResultRelay keeps acknowledgment as its own record with revision binding rather than deriving it from a task status; this is offered as a candidate contribution to the gap discussion.
global_comparator: G3 and G4 are the comparators themselves.
review_needed: yes - standards review needed before any real integration

question: How long must the communication record for a walk-in critical result be retained, and in what form?
what_existing_sources_establish: S1 §9.3.6 cross-refers retention to the DHA Guidelines for Managing Health Records, which were not retrieved or reviewed in this build.
what_remains_unclear: The retention period and format applicable to the communication record are not established by the sources actually reviewed.
technical_consequence: A prototype must not invent a retention period.
proposed_product_control: ResultRelay stores records indefinitely for the lifetime of the demonstration database and states that no retention claim is made.
review_needed: yes - the cross-referenced DHA instrument must be retrieved before any retention claim

question: What should happen when the delivery outcome of a critical-result message is unknown?
what_existing_sources_establish: S1 requires a record of the communication. The US comparator requires the EHR to track order and result status so that problems with delivery can be detected.
what_remains_unclear: No retrieved Dubai clause addresses an indeterminate delivery outcome, or whether a retry is required, permitted, or forbidden while the outcome is unknown.
technical_consequence: A retry may duplicate the message; a suppressed retry may leave the patient uninformed.
proposed_product_control: Explicit DELIVERY_STATE_UNKNOWN state; reconciliation required before retry (INV-4); idempotency keys prevent duplicate sends; escalation when uncertainty persists.
global_comparator: G2 2.1 order tracking is the closest comparator concept for detecting delivery problems.
review_needed: yes - facility-level decision with clinical governance sign-off

question: How long must the communication record for a notified critical result be kept, and who decides when it may be purged?
what_existing_sources_establish: Federal Law 2/2019 Article 20 sets a floor of 25 years from the last health procedure, and DHA HISHD/PP-12 §4.6.1 restates it as an entity obligation, reserving longer-retention decisions to the Executive leader/Medical Director.
what_remains_unclear: Neither instrument says whether a message log is itself a health information asset for retention purposes, or what the retention period is for the communication trail (recipient, channel, timestamps) as distinct from the result.
technical_consequence: The prototype keeps every run, message and audit row in one SQLite file with no retention or purge policy at all. It therefore satisfies neither the floor nor a defensible disposal rule; it simply never deletes.
proposed_product_control: Retention is a schema-level field: every communication and audit record carries a retain_until derived from the last encounter plus the applicable floor, and deletion is a named human action recorded as an event rather than a routine job.
global_comparator: No comparator used; the floor is set nationally.
review_needed: yes - retention of the communication trail (as opposed to the result) is inferred from the definition of a health information asset and needs facility counsel confirmation

question: How does a patient raise, and how does the laboratory receive, a report that a communicated result is wrong?
what_existing_sources_establish: Federal law requires the validity and credibility of health data to be protected against unauthorised amendment; Dubai requires accuracy at record level and requires entities to implement methods to receive patient feedback about inaccurate information; ST-28 requires a corrected report to be identified as revised with date/time and both versions retained.
what_remains_unclear: None of the reviewed instruments prescribes a channel, a response time, or an acknowledgment duty for a patient-initiated correction request. The prototype has no inbound path at all: a patient cannot report an error through it.
technical_consequence: The system can document that a corrected result was re-communicated, but cannot receive the signal that a correction is needed. Correction is only initiable by staff, so the Dubai feedback duty is unmet by the product as built.
proposed_product_control: An inbound correction-request intake that creates a linked case, requires named human adjudication, and never mutates the original communication record - plus an explicit acknowledgement back to the patient. Tracked as GR-14 in the gap register and NOT implemented in this build.
global_comparator: None retrieved that sets a channel or a deadline.
review_needed: no - the absence is established; the channel design is a facility decision
